# Skeema

Skeema is a tool for managing MySQL and MariaDB schema changes in a declarative fashion using pure SQL. The Skeema CLI tool allows you to:

* Export `CREATE TABLE` statements to the filesystem, for tracking in a Git repo
* Diff changes in the schema repo against live DBs to automatically generate DDL
* Manage multiple environments (e.g. dev, staging, prod) and keep them in sync with ease
* Configure use of online schema change tools, such as `pt-online-schema-change`, `gh-ost`, or `spirit`, for performing `ALTER TABLE`
* Apply configurable linter rules to proactively catch schema design problems and enforce company policies

Skeema supports a pull-request-based workflow for schema change submission, review, and execution. This permits your team to manage schema changes in exactly the same way as you manage code changes.

## Products and Downloads

This repo is the free open source Community edition of the Skeema command-line tool. The Community edition supports management of **tables** and **routines** (procs/funcs). Builds are provided for Linux and MacOS.

The paid Premium edition of the Skeema CLI adds support for managing **views**, **triggers**, and **events**. It also includes a native **Windows build**, built-in **SSH tunnel** functionality, **seed data** management, and many other improvements.

For download links and more information, visit [skeema.io](https://www.skeema.io/download/).

import subprocess, os, tempfile
EXE="/workspace/executable"
def run(args, cwd, files=None):
    if files:
        for name,content in files.items():
            p=os.path.join(cwd,name)
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p), exist_ok=True)
            open(p,"w").write(content)
    p=subprocess.run([EXE]+args, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=cwd)
    return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr

def test(desc, files, args):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
        rc,out,err=run(args,td,files)
        print(f"=== {desc} {args} rc={rc}")
        print("out:",out)
        print("err:",err)
        for root,dirs,fs in os.walk(td):
            for f in fs:
                fp=os.path.join(root,f)
                print(" file",os.path.relpath(fp,td),repr(open(fp).read()))

test("lint skip-format valid", {"a.sql":sql}, ["lint","--skip-format"])
test("lint skip-format no pk", {"a.sql":"CREATE TABLE t (id int);\n"}, ["lint","--skip-format"])
test("format skip-write", {"a.sql":sql}, ["format","--skip-write"])

test("lint has float error", {"a.sql":"CREATE TABLE t (id float, PRIMARY KEY(id));\n"}, ["lint","--skip-format","--lint-has-float=error"])
test("lint multiple", {"a.sql":"CREATE TABLE t (id float);\nCREATE TABLE u (x enum('a'));\n"}, ["lint","--skip-format","--lint-has-float=error","--lint-has-enum=warning"])
PY

Usage:  skeema diff [<options>] [<environment>]

Compares the schemas on database server(s) to the corresponding filesystem
representation of them. The output is a series of DDL commands that, if run on
the DB server, would cause its schemas to now match the definitions from the
filesystem.

You may optionally pass an environment name as a command-line arg. This will
affect which section of .skeema config files is used for processing. For
example, running `skeema diff staging` will apply config directives from the
[staging] section of config files, as well as any sectionless directives at the
top of the file. If no environment name is supplied, the default is
"production".

The `skeema diff` command is equivalent to running `skeema push` with its
--dry-run option enabled.

An exit code of 0 will be returned if no differences were found; 1 if some
differences were found; or 2+ if an error occurred.

import subprocess, os, tempfile, sys
EXE="/workspace/executable"
def run_once(args, cwd_files=None, home_files=None, env_extra=None, subcwd=None, stdin=None):
    td=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="CWD_"); home=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="HOME_")
    for base,files in [(td,cwd_files),(home,home_files)]:
        if files:
            for n,c in files.items():
                p=os.path.join(base,n); os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p),exist_ok=True)
                if isinstance(c,bytes): open(p,"wb").write(c)
                else: open(p,"w").write(c)
    env=dict(os.environ); env["HOME"]=home
    if env_extra: env.update(env_extra)
    cwd=os.path.join(td,subcwd) if subcwd else td
    p=subprocess.run([EXE]+args,capture_output=True,text=True,cwd=cwd,env=env,input=stdin)
    # capture resulting files
    res={}
    for root,ds,fs in os.walk(td):
        for f in fs:
            fp=os.path.join(root,f)
            try: res[os.path.relpath(fp,td)]=open(fp).read()
            except: res[os.path.relpath(fp,td)]="<binary>"
    return {"td":td,"home":home,"rc":p.returncode,"out":p.stdout,"err":p.stderr,"files":res}
def show(desc,args,**kw):
    r=run_once(args,**kw)
    fmt=lambda s: s.replace(r["td"],"$DIR").replace(r["home"],"$HOME")
    print(f"=== {desc} {args} rc={r['rc']}")
    if r["out"]: print("out:",repr(fmt(r["out"])))
    print("err:",repr(fmt(r["err"])))
    for k,v in r["files"].items(): print(" file",k,repr(v))
    return r

{"command":"python3 << 'PY'
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,"/tmp"); from harness import show
import os, tempfile, subprocess
# Create wrapper scripts in cwd
for desc, wrapper_content, cfg in [
 ("echo fixed", "#!/bin/sh\necho 127.0.0.1\n", "[production]\nhost=orig\nschema=db\n"),
 ("echo args", "#!/bin/sh\necho \"args:$@\" >&2\necho 127.0.0.1\n", "[production]\nhost=orig\nschema=db\n"),
 ("echo env", "#!/bin/sh\nenv | grep -i skeema\necho 127.0.0.1\n", "[production]\nhost=orig\nschema=db\n"),
 ("fail", "#!/bin/sh\necho someerror >&2\nexit 3\n", "[production]\nhost=orig\nschema=db\n"),
 ("multiple", "#!/bin/sh\necho 127.0.0.1\necho 127.0.0.2\n", "[production]\nhost=orig\nschema=db\n"),
 ("empty output", "#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n", "[production]\nhost=orig\nschema=db\n"),
]:
    td=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="CWD_"); home=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="HOME_")
    # manual because wrapper needs exec chmod
    open(os.path.join(td,".skeema"),"w").write(cfg)
    open(os.path.join(td,"a.sql"),"w").write("CREATE TABLE t (id int);\n")
    wp=os.path.join(td,"wrapper.sh"); open(wp,"w").write(wrapper_content); os.chmod(wp,0o755)
    env=dict(os.environ); env["HOME"]=home
    p=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","diff","--host-wrapper=./wrapper.sh"],capture_output=True,text=True,cwd=td,env=env)
    print(desc, "rc",p.returncode, "err",p.stderr.replace(td,"$DIR"), "out",p.stdout)
# template variables trial: use wrapper that echoes argument substitution if we pass template
for tmpl in ["./wrapper.sh {HOST}", "./wrapper.sh --host={HOST} --port={PORT}", "./wrapper.sh {SCHEMA}", "./wrapper.sh {ENV}", "./wrapper.sh {DIR}"]:
    td=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="CWD_"); home=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="HOME_")
    open(os.path.join(td,".skeema"),"w").write("[production]\nhost=orig\nschema=db\n")
    open(os.path.join(td,"a.sql"),"w").write("CREATE TABLE t (id int);\n")
    wp=os.path.join(td,"wrapper.sh"); open(wp,"w").write("#!/bin/sh\necho \"ARGS:$*\" >&2\n echo 127.0.0.1\n"); os.chmod(wp,0o755)
    env=dict(os.environ); env["HOME"]=home
    p=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","diff",f"--host-wrapper={tmpl}"],capture_output=True,text=True,cwd=td,env=env)
    print("tmpl",tmpl,"rc",p.returncode,"err",p.stderr.replace(td,"$DIR"))
PY
"}

import socket, threading, subprocess, os, tempfile, time
EXE="/workspace/executable"
def serve_once(mode, port_holder):
    srv=socket.socket(); srv.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR,1); srv.bind(("127.0.0.1",0)); srv.listen(5)
    port_holder.append(srv.getsockname()[1])
    def handle():
        srv.settimeout(10)
        try:
            while True:
                conn,addr=srv.accept()
                if mode=="close":
                    conn.close()
                elif mode=="garbage":
                    conn.sendall(b"HELLO NOT MYSQL\n"); time.sleep(0.2); conn.close()
                elif mode=="handshake_garbage":
                    # packet header len 5 seq0 + garbage
                    conn.sendall(b"\x05\x00\x00\x00\xff\xff\xff\xff\xff"); time.sleep(0.2); conn.close()

import subprocess, os, tempfile
EXE="/workspace/executable"
configs={
 "none": "",
 "host": "host=127.0.0.1\n",
 "schema": "schema=db\n",
 "host+schema": "host=127.0.0.1\nschema=db\n",
 "flavor": "flavor=mysql:8.0\nworkspace=docker\n",
}
sqls={"unsupported":"FOO;\n","supported":"CREATE TABLE t (id int);\n","empty":""}
for cmd in ["lint","format","diff","push","pull"]:
  for cname,cfg in configs.items():
    for sname,sql in sqls.items():
      td=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="CWD_"); home=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="HOME_")
      open(os.path.join(td,".skeema"),"w").write("password\n"+cfg)
      open(os.path.join(td,"a.sql"),"w").write(sql)
      env=dict(os.environ); env["HOME"]=home
      p=subprocess.run([EXE,cmd],capture_output=True,text=True,cwd=td,env=env)
      prompt=[l for l in p.stderr.splitlines() if "password" in l.lower()]
      print(cmd,cname,sname,"rc",p.returncode,"prompt",prompt)

import pathlib
p=pathlib.Path("src/skeema_impl.py"); s=p.read_text()
start=s.index("def handle_diff_push(ctx, is_push):")
end=s.index("ctx_env_name_global = [\"production\"]")
new='''def handle_diff_push(ctx, is_push):
    base = get_base_dir(ctx)
    validate_ignore_regexes(base.config)
    validate_concurrent(base.config)
    state = {"problems": 0}
    _diff_process_dir(base, ctx, state, below_target=False, is_base=True)
    problems = state["problems"]
    if problems:
        log_error(f"Skipped {problems} operation{'s' if problems != 1 else ''} due to problem{'s' if problems != 1 else ''}")
        return 2
    return None

def _diff_process_dir(d, ctx, state, below_target, is_base):
    if d.error is not None:
        log_error(f"Skipping {d.path}: {d.error.message}")
        state["problems"] += 1
        return
    if is_base:
        own_cur, own_any = d.schema_present_current, d.schema_present_any
    else:
        own_cur, own_any = d.own_schema_current, d.own_schema_any
    child_below = below_target
    if own_any:
        child_below = True
        if own_cur:
            _diff_process_target(d, ctx, state)
        else:
            log_warn(f"Skipping {d.path}: no schema defined for environment \\"{ctx.env_name}\\"")
            log_warn("Other environments do define a schema name. Refer to the .skeema file in this directory for details.")
    subs = build_subdirs(d, ctx)
    for sub in subs:
        _diff_process_dir(sub, ctx, state, below_target=child_below, is_base=False)

def _diff_process_target(d, ctx, state):
    cfg = d.config
    host = cfg.get("host").strip()
    if host == "":
        log_warn(f"Skipping {d.path}: no host defined for environment \\"{ctx.env_name}\\"")
        if cfg.get("host-wrapper").strip() != "":
            log_warn("The host-wrapper option controls which hosts this directory maps to, but a .skeema file also needs to set the host option to some value (even just a placeholder value) for this command to properly map directories to hosts and schemas.")
        else:
            log_warn(f"This command requires a hostname, which can be specified using the host option in a [{ctx.env_name}] section of the .skeema file in this directory, or in a parent directory.")
        return
    insts, terr = expand_instances_for_target(d, ctx)
    if terr is not None:
        if terr.message == "emptywrapper":
            log_warn(f"Skipping {d.path}: directory maps to an empty list of database servers")
            log_warn("The host-wrapper option controls which hosts this directory maps to, but the executed script returned no hostnames.")
            return
        if terr.message == "nohost":
            log_warn(f"Skipping {d.path}: no host defined for environment \\"{ctx.env_name}\\"")
            log_warn(f"This command requires a hostname, which can be specified using the host option in a [{ctx.env_name}] section of the .skeema file in this directory, or in a parent directory.")
            return
        log_error(f"Skipping {d.path}: {terr.message}")
        state["problems"] += 1
        return
    if d.config.bare("password"):
        labels = " and ".join(f"{inst.user}@{inst.host}" for inst in insts)
        pw, err = prompt_password(f"Enter password for {labels}: ")
        if err is not None:
            log_error(f"Skipping {d.path}: Unable to prompt password for {labels}: {err}")
            state["problems"] += 1
            return
        d.config.set("password", pw, d.config.source_of("password"), 100, bare=False)
        insts2, terr2 = expand_instances_for_target(d, ctx)
        if terr2 is None:
            insts = insts2
    for inst in insts:
        err = attempt_connection(inst)
        if err is not None:
            if err.startswith("Unable to connect") or err.startswith("Invalid"):

            else:
                log_error(f"Skipping {inst} for {d.path}: {err}")
            state["problems"] += 1
            continue

import pathlib
p=pathlib.Path("src/skeema_impl.py"); s=p.read_text()
old_start=s.index("def log_msg(level, message):")
old_end=s.index("def log_info(msg):")
new='''def log_msg(level, message):
    if level == "DEBUG" and not _debug_enabled:
        return
    if message is None:
        message = ""
    pad = " " * max(1, 6 - len(level))
    plain_prefix = f"{_timestamp()} [{level}]{pad}"
    try:
        is_tty = sys.stderr.isatty()
    except Exception:
        is_tty = False
    lines = str(message).split("\\n")
    if is_tty:
        colors = {"INFO": "32", "WARN": "33", "ERROR": "31", "DEBUG": "36"}
        color = colors.get(level, "37")
        colored_prefix = f"{_timestamp()} [\\x1b[1m\\x1b[{color}m{level}\\x1b[0m\\x1b[39m\\x1b[49m]{pad}"
        try:
            width = os.get_terminal_size(sys.stderr.fileno()).columns
        except Exception:
            width = 80
        if width >= 80:
            import textwrap as _tw
            avail = max(20, width - len(plain_prefix))
            out_lines = []
            for physical in lines:
                if physical == "":
                    out_lines.append("")
                    continue
                wrapped = _tw.wrap(physical, width=avail, break_long_words=True, break_on_hyphens=False, expand_tabs=False, replace_whitespace=False, drop_whitespace=True)
                if not wrapped:
                    wrapped = [""]
                out_lines.extend(wrapped)
            for idx, line in enumerate(out_lines):
                if idx == 0:
                    sys.stderr.write(f"{colored_prefix}{line}\\n")
                else:
                    sys.stderr.write(f"{' ' * len(plain_prefix)}{line}\\n")
            sys.stderr.flush()
            return
        for line in lines:
            sys.stderr.write(f"{colored_prefix}{line}\\n")
        sys.stderr.flush()
        return
    for line in lines:
        sys.stderr.write(f"{plain_prefix}{line}\\n")
    sys.stderr.flush()

'''
s=s[:old_start]+new+s[old_end:]
p.write_text(s)

s=s.replace('''def print_help_for(name):''','''def _render_help_dynamic(text, width):
    import textwrap as _tw
    lines = text.split("\\n")
    # Parse into blocks: list of tuples
    # We reconstruct by walking lines and identifying sections
    out = []
    i = 0
    # Usage line + description paragraphs until first heading
    # Generic approach: process "units": paragraphs, headings, entries.
    units = []  # (kind, data)
    cur_para = []
    def flush_para():
        nonlocal cur_para
        if cur_para:
            units.append(("para", " ".join(x.strip() for x in cur_para)))
            cur_para = []
    idx = 0
    entries = []
    in_section = False
    desc_col = None
    def flush_entries():
        nonlocal entries, desc_col
        if entries:
            units.append(("entries", (list(entries), desc_col)))
            entries = []
            desc_col = None
    while idx < len(lines):
        line = lines[idx]
        stripped = line.strip()
        if stripped == "":
            flush_para(); flush_entries(); units.append(("blank", None)); idx += 1; continue
        is_heading = (not line.startswith(" ") and stripped.endswith(":") and len(stripped) < 60 and not stripped.startswith("Usage"))
        if is_heading:
            flush_para(); flush_entries(); units.append(("heading", stripped)); in_section = True; idx += 1; continue
        if in_section:
            # entry start: indented, double-space before description
            m = None
            # find runs of 2+ spaces after a non-space segment
            mm = None
            # description column candidates: position of a 2+ space run followed by nonspace
            for cand in range(1, len(line)-1):
                if line[cand:cand+2] == "  " and line[cand:].strip() != "":
                    # ensure there is nonspace after spaces
                    rest = line[cand:].lstrip()
                    if rest:
                        mm = cand
                        # choose the last such? first run after spec usually
                        break
            if line.startswith(" ") and mm is not None and not line.startswith(" " * 12):
                # start of a new entry if it looks like an option/command line
                spec = line[:mm].rstrip()
                desc = line[mm:].strip()
                if desc_col is None:
                    # determine desc col from the space run end
                    j = mm
                    while j < len(line) and line[j] == " ":
                        j += 1
                    desc_col = j
                entries.append([spec, desc])
                idx += 1; continue
            if entries and line.startswith(" ") and line.strip():
                entries[-1][1] += " " + stripped
                idx += 1; continue
            # fallback: paragraph within section (shouldn't happen)
            flush_entries(); cur_para.append(line); idx += 1; continue
        cur_para.append(line); idx += 1
    flush_para(); flush_entries()
    # Render
    rendered = []
    for kind, data in units:
        if kind == "blank":
            rendered.append("")
        elif kind == "heading":
            rendered.append(data)
        elif kind == "para":
            if data.startswith("Usage:"):
                rendered.append(data)
            else:
                rendered.extend(_tw.wrap(data, width=width, break_long_words=True, break_on_hyphens=False, expand_tabs=False))
        elif kind == "entries":
            ents, dc = data
            if dc is None: dc = 32
            for spec, desc in ents:
                wrapped = _tw.wrap(desc, width=max(20, width-dc), break_long_words=True, break_on_hyphens=False, expand_tabs=False)
                if not wrapped: wrapped = [""]
                rendered.append(spec.ljust(dc) + wrapped[0])
                for cont in wrapped[1:]:
                    rendered.append(" " * dc + cont)
    # Collapse >1 consecutive blanks to 1, preserve single trailing blank structure
    out_lines = []
    prev_blank = False
    for l in rendered:
        if l == "" and prev_blank:
            continue
        out_lines.append(l); prev_blank = (l == "")
    return "\\n".join(out_lines).rstrip("\\n") + "\\n\\n"

def print_help_for(name):''')
# modify print_help_for body
s=s.replace('''def print_help_for(name):
    if name is None:
        sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXTS["main"])
    else:

    sys.stdout.flush()''','''def print_help_for(name):

    sys.stdout.write(text)
    sys.stdout.flush()''')

                out.append(template[i:]); break
            out.append(template[i:end+2]); i = end + 2; continue
        if template[i] == "{":

            if close == -1:
                return None, f"Variable name missing closing brace: {template[i:]}"
            raw = template[i+1:close]
            lookup = raw.rstrip(" \\t").upper()
            if lookup not in variables:
                return None, f"Unknown variable {lookup}"
            out.append(variables[lookup])
            i = close + 1

        out.append(template[i]); i += 1
    command = "".join(out)

import subprocess, os, tempfile, re, pathlib, sys

def discover(candidates, command="lint"):
    candidates=list(dict.fromkeys(candidates))
    known=[]
    remaining=list(candidates)
    while remaining:
        td=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="CWD_"); home=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="HOME_")
        content="\n".join(f"{c}=x" for c in remaining)+"\n"

            # success or other error; all remaining are known (or other parse issues)
            known.extend(remaining)

                print("unexpected",p.returncode,p.stderr[:200])

        if 1 <= line <= len(remaining):
            remaining.pop(line-1)
        else:
            print("line out of range",line,m.group(2),p.stderr); break
    return known

known=discover(cands)
print("KNOWN single words:", known)
